problem: Existing robot simulators and benchmarks offer only dozens of scenes/objects, short-horizon single-scene tasks, weak physics or rendering, and often need sim-training, so they cannot measure generalization over the long tail nor reliably predict real-world performance.
motivation: Generalist zero-shot policies (VLAs) are saturating old benchmarks, and physical evaluation is too slow and small-scale to probe diversity. A large, physically validated, simulator-agnostic ecosystem with strong sim-to-real correlation would allow rigorous large-scale evaluation and diagnosis of failure modes.
key_idea: Build an open, multi-simulator ecosystem of 230k scenes, 130k objects and 42M grasps, and use it to create MolmoSpaces-Bench, an 8-task zero-shot benchmark whose success rates correlate strongly with real-world results.
insight: Sim results can predict real-world policy ranking (pick task Pearson 0.96, Spearman 0.98 against 752 RoboArena episodes), so large-scale sim evaluation is a valid proxy. The perturbation studies expose brittleness: pi0 is within 1% of pi0.5 with DROID-frequent prompts but 14% behind otherwise, suggesting the language conditioning limits earlier models. Occluding the wrist camera drops pi0.5 to 2% versus 20% for third-person occlusion, and success degrades with initial-joint shifts.
method: MolmoSpaces-Scenes: five scene datasets (MSCrafted 120, MSProc 12k, MSProcObja 110k, MSMultiType 110k LLM-generated Holodeck scenes with grid constraint and personas, MSTwin digital twin) converted to MuJoCo/Isaac (USD)/ManiSkill.
Scene quality testing: stability, intersection, lift and articulation tests that remove problematic objects; pass rates mostly >90% in MuJoCo (articulation on MSMultiType is 65.2%).
MolmoSpaces-Objects: 1.6k THOR and 129k curated Objaverse assets with GPT-4o/4.1 annotations (mass, synsets, pickable, receptacle), COACD colliders and multi-stage filtering.
MolmoSpaces-Grasp: 42M Robotiq 2F-85 6-DoF grasps for 48k objects, with rigid slip-perturbation checks, articulated actuation-feasibility checks and in-situ scene collision/lift tests.
Robots and control: Franka FR3 (DROID setup), RB-Y1 mobile bimanual, floating CAP/Robotiq grippers; joint/pose controllers and JAX IK.

MolmoSpaces-Bench: 8 tasks (navigate-to, pick, pick-and-place, place-next-to, place-color, open, close, open-door), 2k solvable, diversity-balanced samples per benchmark with dense rewards; perturbation extensions and LLM-generated long-horizon tasks.

setting.backbone: Evaluated existing policies zero-shot: pi0, pi0-FAST, pi0.5 (DROID joint-position variants), CAP (with Gemini-Robotics-ER-1.5 contact points), RING, DualVLN
setting.training_data: none for the benchmark (evaluated policies are pre-trained by others; no fine-tuning on benchmark data)
setting.observation: Wrist + two third-person RGB(-D) cameras for Franka; head/navigation camera RGB for RB-Y1 navigation; proprioception
setting.action_space: Joint position commands for manipulators; absolute/relative pose for mobile base and floating gripper; navigation with explicit stop signal
setting.privileged: none for policies (benchmark tasks filtered for solvability; CAP contact points come from a VLM)

numbers_note: Policy success rates are reported only in figures (Fig. model_comparison, robustness, sim-to-real); the text gives only correlation values (R=0.96, rho=0.98), a few percentages, and no navigation SR/SPL table.
results: Newer policies outperform earlier ones zero-shot (pi0.5 > pi0-FAST/pi0) on the benchmark, and sim-to-real correlation on pick is R=0.96, rho=0.98. RING outperforms DualVLN on navigate-to, explained by DualVLN's distribution mismatch (detailed instructions vs. semantic goals). Pi models benefit from retries (2.65 grasp-ungrasp transitions for pi0.5 vs 4.63 for pi0).
limitations: Baseline results are shown only in figures, with a limited set of policies; the long-horizon tasks are provided but not evaluated.
Open/close sim-to-real correlations rest on few real episodes and have wide error bars; task filtering for DROID setup may favor Robotiq grippers.
Some scenes have low articulation pass rates (MSMultiType 65.2%), and the prompt-sensitivity finding is validated only for pick.
